prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind O&M; scope Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere), excludes public grid and non-farm port ops. Wildmere: Export Limit Advisory→Grid Dispatcher when capability<target; applies accepted ceiling, records time; keeps protection settings unless authorized switching plan; available during substation work. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): validated commands within protections, blocks conflicts, safe mode on auxiliary loss; Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor→Turbine Sensor Bus. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer, export cable, Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers, Fire Detection Panel; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; uses Switching Window Acknowledgment to confirm window; mode Substation Degraded. Substation Operator switches only when window active, operational authority confirmed, state checked, Control Engineer authorized; notifies Grid Dispatcher. Outage windows: export capacity assessed first; Grid Constraint may shorten/move/split; window covers switching, work, test, restoration without unplanned extensions; Marine Coordinator checks vessel/transfer timing; Electrical Technician confirms scope fits; Work Permit Portal updated before start; delays raised; unsafe/grid-incompatible→pause; revised window before deferred work; restore in authorized sequence; Duty Planner records actual times; availability returned after checks. Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-start on auxiliary loss, no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): telemetry with source timestamps→Shore Control Room (Amber Quay, comms coordination point); Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway. Shore Control Room keeps last validated limit on comms loss; incident log; go/no-go. Operations Radio Console: voice to CTV, SOV, Daughter Craft in coverage; Vessel Master read-back of safety-critical instructions; proceed/hold/withdraw; Transfer Manifest Addendum from Duty Planner. Grid Dispatcher priority safety>protection>export. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard): Position Quality Flag. Mode Grid Constraint: Duty Planner records basis; Control Engineer reduces stepwise, restores after authorization. Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): Squall Window Bulletin, Deferred Task Rationale, replenishment forecasts. Weather Service, Metocean Buoy + offshore observations→Weather Analyst (uncertainty; Wave Burst Record, Visibility Confidence Note)→Duty Planner; Marine Coordinator shares marine/weather info with vessels, Duty Planner. Uncertain=no-go. CTV (Harness Audit Card), SOV (Recovery Basket Load Sheet).

New part:
S768: The Control Engineer reviews alarms and operating trends with the SCADA Engineer when an abnormal condition may require intervention.
S769: The Grid Dispatcher communicates external operating requirements to the Grid Interface Relay and the responsible control personnel.
S770: Instructions that affect electrical safety are communicated through authorized channels and confirmed by the responsible Substation Operator or Electrical Technician.
S771: When a communication channel is unavailable, personnel use the approved fallback method and report the outage as soon as practicable.
S772: Urgent messages identify the affected asset, the hazard or condition, the required action, and the person issuing the instruction.
S773: The receiver repeats critical details, and the sender confirms that the read-back is accurate before the instruction is treated as understood.
S774: Operational records identify the originator, recipient, event time, recording time, relevant asset, and decision or action taken.
S775: Entries distinguish observed facts from estimates, assumptions, and recommendations so that later reviewers can assess their basis.
S776: Records use synchronized time sources where available, and any known clock discrepancy is noted for later reconciliation.
S777: Corrections preserve the original entry, identify the person making the change, and state the reason for the correction.
S778: The Field Supervisor ensures that field observations and work outcomes are entered promptly while the details remain verifiable.
S779: The Duty Planner links relevant communications and work records to the applicable work package and operating plan.
S780: The Work Permit Portal retains permit decisions and associated approvals in a form that can be retrieved for review.
S781: The Cybersecurity Analyst protects access logs and communication records against unauthorized alteration or disclosure.
S782: The organization retains voice recordings, system logs, and work records according to the approved retention schedule and applicable legal obligations.
S783: Records subject to an investigation, claim, or safety review are preserved from routine deletion until the authorized release of the hold.
S784: The responsible manager reviews record completeness after significant events and assigns correction or follow-up actions where evidence is missing.
S785: Fire protection is designed to detect smoke, heat, and flame early enough to support automatic equipment protection and a controlled personnel response.
S786: The Fire Detection Panel supervises detection circuits and annunciates alarms with location and fault information.
S787: Detection coverage includes electrical enclosures, machinery spaces, and other areas identified by the site fire risk assessment.
S788: The Turbine Sensor Bus carries equipment status used by protective functions and operational monitoring.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
